title: Proportional burst allocation and post-facto billing adjustments for Dedicated capacity
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: Dedicated pools expose reserved throughput (committed capacity) plus opportunistic burst capacity. When pool degradation or preemption occurs we must: 1) fairly attribute reserved vs burst usage per tenant; 2) apply SLA credits if reserved throughput was degraded; and 3) offer deterministic, auditable post-facto billing adjustments so finance and customers can reconcile invoices. Current implementation uses a best-effort leaky-bucket per-tenant counter and applies burst credits at coarse windows which leads to noisy attributions and occasional overcharges during multi-tenant pool events. This ticket designs and implements a proportional, time-sliced usage ledger and a reconciliation job that computes SLA credits and negative-balance adjustments after the fact.
goal: Create a deterministic, time-sliced ledger for Dedicated pools that: (a) attributes reserved vs burst consumption proportionally across tenants for each time-slice; (b) computes SLA credit allocation and negative-balance protections post-facto; (c) is idempotent, auditable, and compatible with existing billing pipelines.
proposal_summary: Introduce 1-minute time-sliced ingestion of pool-level telemetry and per-tenant request tokens. For each minute slice, compute theoretical reserved entitlement per tenant (based on their committed throughput at that minute) and classify actual tokens consumed into reserved vs burst proportions using a proportional allocator when aggregate demand > reserved capacity. Persist ledger rows per-tenant per-minute. Run a daily reconciliation job to calculate SLA credits for minutes where actual available capacity < reserved capacity and to generate post-facto adjustments (credits/debits) exposed to billing. Implement a shadow mode for 6 weeks before enabling adjustments to invoices.
design_notes: Telemetry ingestion: use existing runtime metrics endpoint to emit pool.available_capacity and per-tenant.request_tokens per 10s, aggregate into 1m buckets in the ingestion service.

Allocation algorithm: for each minute M, let R = sum(reserved_capacity_i) for tenants i, A = available_capacity_observed for the pool, and T_i = tokens_consumed_by_tenant_i in M. If sum(T_i) <= R then mark consumption as reserved up to each tenant's reserved share. If sum(T_i) > R then compute reserved_share_i = min(T_i, floor(R * (reserved_capacity_i / R))) and remaining tokens are burst. When reserved_capacity floats (reassignments), use the committed reservation snapshot at minute boundary.

SLA credit calc: for minutes where A < R_expected (expected reserved pool capacity), compute an availability_ratio = A / R_expected. For each tenant, SLA_credit_minutes = (1 - availability_ratio) * reserved_share_i. Convert SLA minutes into monetary credit using the tenant's reserved unit rate at invoice time.

Ledger schema (persisted): one row per tenant per-minute with fields: timestamp_minute, tenant_key, reserved_entitled, tokens_consumed, reserved_attributed, burst_attributed, pool_id, capacity_snapshot_tag. Stored in OLAP as CSV/Parquet and exported to billing pipeline. (Persisted as flat columns; no nested blobs.)

Idempotency: reconciliation job computes adjustments by looking up ledger rows with reconciliation_tag=NULL and emits adjustments with a deterministic hash. If a run fails, it can safely retry without double-applying adjustments.

Performance: aggregation and allocation done inside a streaming job (Flink/kafka-streams) with local in-memory per-pool windowed state to operate at scale. Output to an events topic consumed by reconciliation worker.
Auditability: generate per-adjustment proof payload (ledger_rows included by id) linked in billing records and customer-facing invoice adjustments UI.

Compatibility: provide mapping from new ledger rows to existing billing pipeline fields so finance reports remain consistent. Add feature flag to toggle applying adjustments to invoices while still writing ledger rows.

Edge cases: short spikes (<1s) are captured in 1m buckets; preemption mid-minute uses capacity_snapshot_tag to ensure visibility and later correction via SLA credit logic. Pool split/merge operations include a migration mapping table to re-anchor ledger rows when pool topology changes.
tradeoffs: Bucket granularity: 1-minute buckets are chosen as a balance between accuracy and storage/compute cost. Finer buckets (10s) increase accuracy for short preemptions but increase ingestion and storage by ~6x.

Proportional allocation fairness vs. simple first-come attribution: proportional approach is fairer for multi-tenant events but requires committed-reservation snapshots per-minute which increases complexity.
Real-time billing adjustments are avoided; we prefer batch post-facto adjustments to keep invoicing deterministic and allow dispute handling.
Shadow-mode complexity: running two parallel attribution models (current production + new ledger) doubles some compute but is necessary for confidence before switching invoice application.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming ingestion emits per-pool 1m buckets with pool_capacity and per-tenant tokens_consume metrics with >=99.9% success under normal load
Allocation job produces ledger rows for 95% of tenant-minute combinations (allowing small data loss windows) and ledger row schema is exported to billing pipeline consumer test harness
Reconciliation daily job computes SLA credits deterministically and produces adjustments with a deterministic hash; two identical runs on the same input produce identical outputs
Shadow-mode comparison: after 4 weeks of shadow runs, discrepancies between old and new attribution are within expected bounds and documented; finance approves cutover criteria

System-level invariants: sum(reserved_attributed + burst_attributed) == tokens_consumed for all ledger rows, and sum(reserved_attributed) <= pool_reserved_capacity for each minute accounting for rounding tolerances
End-to-end e2e integration test that simulates a pool-wide degradation produces SLA credits visible in test-billing UI and an associated audit trail link
implementation_plan: Phase 0: Instrumentation (2w) - ensure runtime emits per-tenant tokens and pool capacity at 10s resolution and add aggregator that writes 1m buckets to topic

Phase 1: Allocation service + ledger writer (3w) - implement proportional allocator in streaming job, write ledger to OLAP and events topic, enable feature flag to start writing rows in production (shadow)
Phase 2: Reconciliation job + billing adapter (2w) - daily job that reads ledger rows, computes SLA credits and adjustments, writes adjustments to billing microservice with idempotency keys
Phase 3: Shadow validation (6w) - run alongside existing system, produce discrepancy dashboards, run stakeholder reviews (Finance, Customer Success, Legal)
Phase 4: Controlled cutover (2w) - enable invoice application for a pilot tenant cohort, monitor closely, then full rollout
Phase 5: Backfill and audit (3w) - backfill historical ledger for rolling window (30d) as allowed by compute budget; apply agreed-upon retroactive credits only after legal/finance sign-off
testing_plan: Unit tests around allocation math (including edge rounding cases)
Property-based tests that assert conservation of tokens across synthetic request traces
Integration test that boots a small dedicated pool in staging and replays recorded production traces to verify ledger outputs
Chaos tests: simulate short preemptions and host-level degradation to validate SLA credit paths
Billing pipeline integration tests that consume adjustments and verify idempotency and balance preservation
monitoring_and_alerting: Metric: daily_total_adjustment_amount > threshold -> pager to finance-runbook
Dashboard: per-pool discrepancy between old_attribution and new_attribution distributions
Audit logs: reconcile_job_run_id and list of ledger row ids included; unprocessed rows metric
migration_and_rollout_notes: Start as write-only: ledger rows are produced but do not feed billing; run shadow comparisons and produce weekly reports for Finance
Pilot tenants: choose 3 mid-size tenants that represent different reservation topologies for invoice pilot
Backfill window: default to 30 days; longer backfill requires manual approval from Finance due to invoice exposure
Dispute handling: adjustments include a human-review flag and can be suppressed until manual approval for enterprise customers
Rollback: feature flag to disable automatic invoice application; ledger rows can continue to be written for forensics
open_questions: Should monetary conversion for SLA minutes use the reservation rate at invoice issue date or at the minute timestamp? (Finance preference: invoice issue date to simplify accounting)
Rounding policy for fractional token attribution when many tenants share a pool — use deterministic floor-with-remainder distribution?
How to show micro-credits on customer invoices without confusing UX — condensed line items vs. aggregated monthly credit?
Policy for retroactive credits older than billing cutoff (e.g., >90 days) — require legal sign-off?
risks: Storage and compute costs increase due to per-minute ledger rows (estimated +15% infra cost for ingestion and OLAP storage)
Finance or Legal objections during audit of historical adjustments that could delay backfill/cutover
Complexity in mapping pool topology changes (split/merge) to existing ledger rows could cause orphaned rows if mapping not recorded
Incorrect implementation could double-credit or double-debit invoices if reconciliation idempotency keys are not robust
